detaileddescription.para: The example initializes the XDMA PCIe IP and shows how to enumerate the PCIe system.

This example should be used only when the XDMA PCIe IP is configured as a root complex. This code will illustrate how the XDmaPcie IP and its standalone driver can be used to:
Initialize a XDMA PCIe IP core built as a root complex
Enumerate PCIe end points in the system
Assign BARs to end points
find capabilities on end point
Please note that this example enumerates and initializes PCIe end points only.

On CPM6 (versal_2vp) the example also drives the PCIe PERST# fundamental reset before enumerating. PERST# is active low and is routed to two pins per controller: a PS MIO pin, driven through the PS_GPIO registers directly because that device tree node is disabled, and a PMC GPIO pin driven through the XGpioPs driver. The pins for the controller in use are selected from the device tree compatible string.

We tried to use as much of the driver's API calls as possible to show the reader how each call could be used and that probably made the example not the shortest way of doing the tasks shown as they could be done.
